supporting_observations.claim: Near the alert time, WS-HITO-01 communicated with DC-RB-01 over LDAP. These records establish connectivity, not the scheduled task's name, creator, action, or authorization.

At 13:42:10 and 13:42:14 UTC, the domain controller recorded service-ticket requests by WS-HITO-01$ for FILE-RB-01$. These requests do not identify an installer path or demonstrate that the alerted task performed the planned deployment.

msiexec.exe accessed services.exe before and after the collection outage, but these process-access records do not provide its command line or link it to the alerted task. They are insufficient to validate a VetChart deployment.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied collection-status metadata reports that WS-HITO-01 Windows Security and Sysmon logs were not collected from 13:30 through 14:15 UTC, encompassing the reported task registration around 13:41 UTC.
The supplied evidence contains no task-registration record or task definition identifying the alerted task's name, author, principal, trigger, or executable action.
Available network and domain-controller records provide surrounding activity but cannot substitute for the missing task definition and endpoint execution history.
claims_not_established: Whether the alerted task matched the approved \RB-IT\Deploy-<App> naming convention and ran msiexec against an installer in \\FILE-RB-01\Deploy.
Whether dev.sharma created or authorized the task as part of the planned VetChart 4.2 deployment.
Whether the task executed successfully, established malicious persistence, or launched any malicious payload.
Whether the FILE-RB-01$ service-ticket requests were associated with the alerted task rather than other workstation activity.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover the original alert payload and task-registration event, including task XML, task name, creator identity, registration time, execution principal, triggers, and actions.
Collect the task definition from WS-HITO-01 and recover retained Windows Security and Task Scheduler Operational logs covering 13:20–14:20 UTC.
Obtain task execution history, associated process command lines and ancestry, and MSI installation logs.
Correlate the deployment change record and dev.sharma's administrative activity with the exact task and installer; verify the installer path, hash, and signature.
Collect FILE-RB-01 share-access records to determine whether WS-HITO-01 accessed the approved deployment installer.
unrelated_findings: Separate software-policy review: Zoom.exe launched as hana.ito and Firefox retrieved Zoom meeting web content. Zoom is not listed among approved software/services in the supplied inventory. These records do not establish a relationship to the scheduled task or malicious activity (S23-00003, S23-00004, S23-00029, S23-00034).

Separate software-policy verification: a proxy connection to secure-client-updates.cisco.com used a Cisco Secure Client/5.1.4 user agent. This service is not listed in the supplied approved inventory; the proxy record alone does not establish installation, remote access, or a relationship to the task (S23-00142).
